reviews.decision_reason: select_demand is the localized behavioral fault. Its visible source selects every corpus row with demand_score >= 3, which includes all 8 supplied records, while the assigned job output contains only the deterministic top record n06-r01. This broad threshold would admit weaker and unrelated candidates instead of preserving the required selected demand path for the deterministic recommendation.

normalize preserves the overly broad selected set it receives. Its code only reindexes, fills missing values, filters to allowed corpus identifiers, and keeps the bounded window of 8, so the observed 8-row normalized output is consistent with upstream over-selection rather than an independently localized fault.

assemble_provenance deterministically ranks the normalized rows by demand_score descending and record_id, with missing-safe field access. The visible 8-row provenance output follows from the 8-row normalized input, so there is no localized evidence that this boundary created the over-selection, but its final artifact remains contaminated by the upstream fault.
